title: Clarify model-binding rules for tags, semver ranges, and commit hashes in SDK/API
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Teams need precise, predictable semantics when they pin a model in the Redwood API/SDK. Current behavior has a few ambiguous resolutions (tag names that match semver, implicit 'latest' fallbacks, and silent resolution that hides what was actually served). This causes flakiness for customers when a new model build is published and a previously-working pin starts returning a different binary with different perf characteristics.

Goal / scope:
- Define a deterministic resolution order for model pins supplied via the API or SDK (pin field on deploy/create calls and run-time calls that accept a model spec).
- Ensure the platform returns the resolved model version id and a compact resolution_trace explaining why a particular version was chosen.
- Publish SDK helpers for pin expressions (tag, semver exact, semver range, commit hash, channel) that mirror server-side logic and can validate pins client-side before API call.
- Make publishing of performance profiles attach to an immutable model_version_id (not a tag) and document how profiles map to pin expressions.

Proposed semantics (server-side resolver):
1) If the pin is a 40+ hex commit hash (commit:<hash> or implicitly detected) => resolve to the exact model_version_id built from that commit. If commit not found => error.
2) If the pin is an exact semver (e.g., 1.3.2 or v1.3.2) => resolve to the exact release matching that version. If not found => error (no silent fallback).
3) If the pin is a semver range (e.g., ^1.3.0, >=1.2 <2.0) => pick the highest compatible release according to semver precedence among published releases. If none matches => error.
4) If the pin is a tag string (e.g., "stable", "experimental", or an arbitrary tag) => resolve to the release currently associated with that tag. Tag resolution is: return the tag->model_version mapping recorded at the moment of resolution. If tag is missing => error.
5) Special channel keywords: "latest" and "channel:stable" are treated as tags (not semver ranges). They must be explicit strings; legacy inputs that were implicitly treated as latest will now require explicit 'latest' (migration path below).
6) If no pin provided, follow call-site defaults: deployment-level default model (if present) otherwise system default.

Precedence note: order above is not fallthrough (i.e., exactly-matching formats are required). We avoid guessing (e.g., a tag that looks like a semver is treated as a tag unless the caller explicitly prefixes with semver: or commit:). This is intentional to reduce accidental resolution changes.

API changes (surface):
- Deploy / Run endpoints accept a new optional field "pin_expression" (string) with the same grammar used by SDKs. Existing "model" string param remains supported but is deprecated when ambiguous; server will accept but return a deprecation warning in resolution_trace.
- Response payload includes these new string fields: "resolved_model_version_id" and "resolution_trace". Both are strings: resolved_model_version_id is the immutable id we use for serving and perf-profile lookup; resolution_trace is a short comma-separated trace like "commit:abcd1234 -> exact-match" or "semver:^1.3.0 -> selected 1.3.7".
- 4xx returned when pin cannot be resolved (instead of silently returning a different model). This is breaking for callers who relied on implicit fallbacks; see migration below.

SDK changes (surface):
- Add PinExpression class/helper with parse(), validate_locally(known_releases), and to_api_payload() helpers. This lets clients 1) detect likely mis-typed pins, 2) warn on ambiguous strings (e.g., 'v1' vs. '^1.0').
- SDKs will expose a resolvePreview(pin_expression) debug helper (non-production) that calls a server preview endpoint to show the exact version that would be selected and the resolution_trace. This requires auth and is rate-limited.
- SDKs will propagate resolution_trace into logs and can optionally raise an exception when resolution differs from a pinned commit (configurable behavior).

Performance profile publishing and mapping:
- Performance profiles are tied to an immutable model_version_id. When a user publishes a perf profile they must reference a model_version_id. The Console UI will allow users to attach a profile to a tag for convenience; this creates a mapping but the profile remains bound to the underlying version id.
- On resolution, if the call used a tag or semver range that mapped to a version with an associated profile, the response includes profile_id and profile_revision (both strings) so SDKs can surface cost and latency expectations.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- Transition window: runtime-1.22 will enable strict resolution mode behind feature-flag for 2 weeks. During this window, responses include an additional warning in resolution_trace when a previously-accepted ambiguous pin would have implicitly resolved to something else.
- Deprecation: ambiguous uses (e.g., calling model="v1" without semver: or tag:) will be accepted for one release with a warning; after that calls will fail with 400. Document migration steps and provide an SDK lint tool to find ambiguous usages in codebases.

Acceptance criteria (must be true to close ticket):
- Server resolver implements the grammar and precedence above and returns resolved_model_version_id and resolution_trace in all successful pin resolutions.
- SDKs (python + node) implement PinExpression helpers and resolvePreview endpoint usage.
- Perf-profile publish flow binds profile to model_version_id and Console shows mapping.
- Integration tests cover commit, exact semver, semver-range, tag, latest, and missing cases with expected 2xx or 4xx responses.
- Documentation + migration guide published in /docs/model-onboarding/pin-semantics.md and linked from Console UI.

Open design trade-offs and risks:
- Strictness vs. ergonomics: making pin resolution strict reduces surprises but increases migration surface. We mitigate by a short flag-guarded rollout and by tooling to find ambig pins.
- Telemetry cost: exposing resolution_trace increases log volume; we plan to keep trace compact (single-line) and sample for high-volume customers.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests: resolver logic, semver precedence, tag lookup, commit exact-match behavior.
- Integration tests: end-to-end create-deployment and run-call that show resolution_trace and actual serving version of the model.
- Perf tests: confirm that publishing a new model_version_id with different quantization does not accidentally map to old perf profiles.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement server + SDK changes behind feature flag.
2) Smoke tests and internal dogfood for 48 hours.
3) Opt-in beta for selected customers with migration support.
4) Flip feature flag to strict mode for all accounts; monitor errors and provide fast rollback path.

Notes on docs & UX wording for Console:
- Console will show the resolved_model_version_id and a short human-friendly sentence: "Resolved to 1.3.7 (release) via semver range ^1.3.0" and a link to the perf profile if present.

Links to artifacts and references are in attachments field below.
